WATCH THE VIDEO OR READ THE ILLUSTRATED RULES Summary and Links In Mattock, you play miners digging corridors through the rock. You can’t dig too closely together though, or the mine will collapse. The last player who is able to mine wins. Mattock's rules are best with illustrations . 3-minute rules video . Goal Trap your opponent so they run out of space to mine. Player Turn THE RULES ARE CONFUSING WITHOUT ILLUSTRATIONS. WATCH THE VIDEO OR READ THE ILLUSTRATED RULES Each player starts with 3 miners on specific places on the board. On your turn, take these 3 steps in order: Mine Place 1 tile on an open space connected to one of your miners by an unbroken series of tiles. Opponent miners block connections. No tile on the board may touch more than 3 other tiles. So the tile you place must not touch: more than 3 other tiles; or a tile which already touches 3 other tiles. If you have any miners which were removed on previous turns, place 1 of them on this tile. If you cannot Mine, you lose the game. THE RULES ARE CONFUSING WITHOUT ILLUSTRATIONS. WATCH THE VIDEO OR READ THE ILLUSTRATED RULES Move You may choose to move any 1 of your miners to a tile connected to it. You do not have to move. You may move through your own miners, but opponent miners block your path. Remove Remove all opponent miners that are now both: not connected to another opponent miner; connected to 2 or more of your miners. BASICALLY: Any miner that's alone in enemy territory gets removed. Your opponent takes the removed miner(s) and will place 1 back on the board on their turn. Never remove your own miners on your turn. THE RULES ARE CONFUSING WITHOUT ILLUSTRATIONS. [Rating: 4/10] I used to dislike any abstract that required too much thinking about what the opponent might do. I've gotten over that. But I still hold the need for that sort of thinking against Mattock... not because I don't want to think about my opponent as such, but because processing which moves are even possible is a pain. It's a pain when looking at the board as it is, and it's a bigger pain when thinking about what would be legal in multiple potential outcomes of a given possible move. [Rating: 5/10] I've only played on a hexhex5 so far. I'm currently on a hexhex7 which may change my mind. As-is I found this one a bit dull and boring. The idea is interesting and unique, however the game tends to push itself to a resolved state rather early, and the rest is going through motions.  EDIT: Much, much better on a larger board than a hex5. There is actually some tussle for how to cut up the board in a hex7 which is simply lacking in a hex5.

[Rating: 5/10] The theme in this abstract game is rather obtuse, but a lot of abstract games don't even have theme. The goal is to be the last player with valid moves. Each player has three miners. On your turn you must first dig a new tile up. It has to be adjacent to a tunnel one of your miners can reach without being blocked by your opponent's miner. It can be any distance away. No dug tile can ever be adjacent to three other dug tiles.
